notes: Identity assessment: title and authors Alexander F. Schmidt and Lisa M. Kistemaker match the neutral replication reference. Title page labels the document Accepted for Publication in COGNITION and supplies an in-press citation; this is a full primary accepted manuscript with methods, results and references, not an abstract or secondary report. The supplied DOI is not printed in the manuscript and the final volume/year/pagination cannot be independently confirmed within this cache-only scope. Manuscript page numbers differ from the supplied p.5 locator: manuscript p.5 is introductory criticism, whereas Study 2 results are pp.13–17. No PDF was supplied. Target ambiguity: Study 2 reports multiple Bonferroni-adjusted dependent-sample post hoc contrasts. On p.13 these include upright vs. inverted males t(59) = 5.18, p < .001; upright vs. inverted females t(59) = 1.22, p = .23; inverted females vs. males t(59) = 3.91, p < .001; and upright females vs. males t < 1 (no individual p printed). Pp.15–16 additionally report counterbalanced female t(59) = 2.82, p = .006 and male t(59) = -1.16, p = .25 contrasts. The description does not select a gender, orientation, or stimulus setup and mentions objects although no actual object category is tested. No test statistic/p pair can be uniquely assigned. Candidate common participant sample: Sixty adults in §4.1 (p.12); participants completed the recognition task in both stages. No exclusion count is documented in that section. This is a candidate common-model N for parent field-scope review only, not a confirmed analytic N for a uniquely matched post hoc target. N is not inferred from t degrees of freedom. Unassigned fields are placeholders only; no original-source or narrative-success extraction was assigned.
